The stem is a SHORTENED form of the correct P26 stem (drops 'En la vivienda en donde usted'), not a stem borrowed from a neighbouring question (the batch_500 p32a trap checked for and absent). Rows a-d equal the questionnaire P26 row text exactly; p26e's .dta label is a DIFFERENT WORDING ('personal remunerado del hogar', paid household staff) from the questionnaire and the Diccionario ('servicio doméstico (personas que reciben un pago por limpiar, lavar, planchar; jardinero, chofer particular)') -- same referent, the administered questionnaire wording is shipped. The CEEY Diccionario xlsx gives 'En la vivienda en donde usted vivía cuando tenía 14 años, ¿tenían…?: <letter>) <row>', identical to the questionnaire stem and rows, 5/5. All asserted in .cache/mexico_2023_mobility_utilities/build.R against pdftotext -raw output. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = questionnaire P26 row text verbatim, row letter stripped, lower-case as printed, p26e's three printed lines joined with single spaces. Note P26d prints '(boiler o solar)' where the current-dwelling twin P95d (sibling _services) prints '(boiler, solar)'; each transcribed as printed. instructions = the P26 stem verbatim, question number dropped: 'En la vivienda en donde usted vivía cuando tenía 14 años, ¿tenían…?' (ellipsis U+2026 as printed). One stem for all rows -> instructions; section_prompt blank; one trivial section_id. Not shipped: interviewer direction 'ROTE Y LEA TODAS LAS OPCIONES' and the CRUCE column marker (batch_496-502 precedent); the heading 'SERVICIOS DE LA VIVIENDA' and the Sección II lead-in are named in the instrument field only. No show card for P26 in the Tarjetas PDF. No source typo in the shipped text. OPTIONS: .dta value labels identical on all five: 1 'Sí', 2 'No', 8 'NS'; the questionnaire grid prints Sí / No / NS (ESP.) over 1 / 2 / 8. SENTINEL: the .do recodes 8 (spontaneous don't-know) to missing and drops it, so resp {1,2} ships with both option rows per item (10 rows); every item uses both levels. Code-8 counts dropped (of 17843 records, 0 system-missing): p26a 28, b 11, c 13, d 54, e 70 -- 176 cells, at most 0.4% per item; no respondent answered 8 on all five, so all 17843 ids are present. REBUILD, decisive: reading entrevistado_2023.dta (id = row number) and dropping 8 as the .do does reproduces the live table exactly: 89039 rows both (= 5 x 17843 - 176), 17843 ids both, 0 resp and 0 cov_age mismatches over 89039 merged id-item rows, cov_sex 1:1 (1=Hombre 39399 rows, 2=Mujer 49640; live stores the label), item x resp cross-tab identical cell for cell (p26a 13565/4250, b 16111/1721, c 12158/5672, d 7864/9925, e 1191/16582) (.cache/mexico_2023_mobility_utilities/rebuild.R; live read from the local irw cache populated by table_context.R, no new export). Content coherent: electricity 90.3%, piped water 76.1%, indoor bathroom 68.2%, water heater 44.2%, domestic service 6.7% 'Sí'. STEP 3b: dictionary Description 'Dwelling services in household of origin' and the .do header ('utilities (P26a to P26e, dwelling services at age 14)') match P26 (recall at age 14), not P95 ('¿En esta vivienda tienen...?', current dwelling, batch_502 sibling mexico_2023_mobility_services), which prints the same five rows with no NS column; the rebuild from the p26 columns reproducing live (and the live table carrying 176 fewer rows than 5 x 17843, whereas P95 has no sentinels) settles it. 5 items and resp 1..2 match. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (5 items, resp 1,2). language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation (CEEY publishes the questionnaire in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by IRW; issues-page line owed once live). RIGHTS: silence. No instrument_rights_register.csv row covers ESRU-EMOVI/CEEY; grep of pdftotext output of the questionnaire and Tarjetas PDFs for copyright/©/derechos reservados/licen/términos de uso/prohib finds only 'licenciatura' (education-level response options); same finding as batch_499-502 siblings. The items are CEEY's own survey questions, no upstream instrument. Extracted under silence-is-permission; ship-shaped, so no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). No other table's files touched.
public_note: Recalled for age 14 (services in the dwelling where the respondent lived then; the current-dwelling version of the same question is mexico_2023_mobility_services); spontaneous don't-know answers are stored as missing (under 0.4% per item); items were read aloud in rotated order; item text English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only ESRU-EMOVI 2023 questionnaire

TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the cues3119.pdf P.22 grid rows, which equal the SPSS labels once the questionnaire's line-break hyphenations are rejoined ('alum-na', 'lle-var', 'con-tra', 'legalmen te', 'come-tan') and the leading bullet dash and dot leaders dropped. instructions = the P.22 stem verbatim ('En general, y pensando en todos los casos posibles, ¿a Ud. le parece muy, bastante, poco o nada aceptable que...?'), asserted as an exact substring of pdftotext -raw output; no show card covers P.22 (tarjetas3119.pdf cards are A-P for P.5-P.50b plus scale/vote/labour/income cards). One trivial section. OPTIONS: ES3119 VALUE LABELS identical on P2201-P2204: 1 'Muy aceptable' 2 'Bastante aceptable' 3 'Poco aceptable' 4 'Nada aceptable' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.'; the questionnaire column headers abbreviate these ('Muy acept.' .. 'Nada acept.'), option_text ships the unabbreviated value labels. No volunteered/NO LEER code exists on P.22. SENTINELS: the .do recodes 8/9 to missing only; dropped per item (8/9): p2201 104/23, p2202 169/14, p2203 216/19, p2204 136/19 (5.1-9.5% of 2470); 16 records answered no item and are absent. Direction: 1 = Muy aceptable (low code = more acceptable), as CIS codes it. REBUILD, decisive: reading DA3119 (2470 records, width 320; id = row number) at cols 100-103, dropping 8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 164 and cov_age cols 165-166 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 9180 rows both, 2454 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as Stata value label (Hombre 4508 / Mujer 4672 rows, no cross cells). Live item x resp (1/2/3/4): p2201 525/876/599/343, p2202 332/589/799/567, p2203 370/693/781/391, p2204 886/807/404/218; means 2.30/2.70/2.50/2.02 -- every item uses all four levels. Content-coherent: the two religion items (p2202 headscarf, p2203 mosque) intercorrelate highest (r=0.61; other pairs 0.34-0.48), and expelling legal immigrants who commit any crime (p2204) is the most accepted. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Acceptability of preferring a Spaniard in hiring, excluding a pupil for wearing a headscarf, protesting against a mosque and expelling legal immigrants who commit crimes') and the .do header ('acceptability (P2201 to P2204)') both describe P.22; 4 items and resp 1..4 match. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (4 items, resp sets exact). language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation (CIS publishes Estudio 3119 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by IRW; 'Bastante aceptable' rendered 'Fairly acceptable', 'Poco aceptable' 'Not very acceptable'; issues-page line owed once live). source_ref: Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS), Estudio 3119 'Actitudes hacia la inmigración (VIII)' (Convenio with OBERAXE; fieldwork 19 noviembre - 1 diciembre 2015 per Ft3119.pdf), N=2470 records. note: mapping_basis=data_labels. DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2015_immigration.do infixes DA3119 at p101 29 p102 30 p103 31 p104 32, identical to ES3119 DATA LIST line 3 (P101 29 .. P104 32) and to the questionnaire's column markers (29)..(32) printed on each P.1 grid row; Bookmark 1 sets item = the (lower-case) CIS variable name -- nothing positional, Step 5b exempt, no verification_/verify_ files written. LABELS: ES3119 VARIABLE LABELS lines 32-35 (/P101 'Personas mayores que viven solas', /P102 'Pensionistas', /P103 'Parados/as', /P104 'Inmigrantes') are string-identical to the four shipped item_text values and to the questionnaire's P.1 grid rows, 4/4 (asserted in .cache/spain_2015_immigration_assistance/build.R). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the cues3119.pdf P.1 grid row labels, bullet dash and leader dots dropped; row 1 is hyphenated across two lines ('vi-/ven solas') and joined. instructions = the P.1 stem verbatim (pdftotext -raw, wraps joined by one space, 'P.1' number dropped): 'Le voy a leer ... protección por parte del Estado.' One stem shared by all four rows, so it sits in instructions; section_prompt blank; one trivial section_id. No show card applies (tarjetas3119.pdf cards start at PREG. 5). Note the stem asks about 'protección por parte del Estado'; the dictionary Description's 'protection or assistance' is a gloss. OPTIONS: ES3119 VALUE LABELS identical on P101-P104: 1 'Mucha' 2 'Bastante' 3 'Poca' 4 'Ninguna' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.'; the questionnaire grid header prints the same four read options (Mucha / Bas-tante / Poca / Ninguna, hyphen joined) plus NS NC. Direction: 1 = Mucha (most protection) .. 4 = Ninguna, as the source codes it. SENTINELS: the .do recodes only 8 (N.S.) and 9 (N.C.) to missing and drops them; there is no NO LEER / volunteered code on P.1, so resp {1..4} ships with four option rows per item (16 rows). Dropped 8/9 per item: p101 175/33 (8.4% of 2470), p102 109/37 (5.9%), p103 134/45 (7.2%), p104 266/45 (12.6%); 46 records answered none of the four and are absent (2424 ids). REBUILD, decisive: reading DA3119 (2470 records; id = row number) at cols 29-32, dropping 8/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex = p44 col 164 and cov_age = p45 cols 165-166 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 9036 rows both, 2424 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt id-item-resp keys, 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as Stata value label (Hombre 4380 / Mujer 4656 rows, no cross cells) (.cache/spain_2015_immigration_assistance/rebuild.R; live read from the local irw cache populated by table_context.R, no extra export). Live item x resp (1/2/3/4): p101 18/243/1601/400, p102 23/415/1597/289, p103 21/279/1454/537, p104 364/833/774/188 -- every item uses every level. Means p101 3.05, p102 2.93, p103 3.09, p104 2.36: content-coherent -- immigrants (p104) are the only group a sizeable share (16.9%) say receive 'mucha' protection, while older people living alone and the unemployed are seen as least protected. Screener: P.0 ends the interview for 'Otra nacionalidad', so all 2470 records are Spanish nationals (P0 1 = 2406, 2 = 64). STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Perceived amount of protection or assistance received by older people living alone, pensioners, the unemployed and immigrants') and the .do header ('assistance (P101 to P104)') both describe P.1; 4 items and resp 1..4 match. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (4 items, resp 1..4). language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation (CIS publishes Estudio 3119 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by IRW; 'Parados/as' rendered 'Unemployed people'; issues-page line owed once live). RIGHTS: applied the existing instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, widened to every CIS survey year 2026-09-23, irw#2381); originator is CIS. No register row written. Sibling spain_2015_immigration_acceptability (in flight this round) and the pending spain_2015_immigration_* tables not touched.
